title: greet.sh should take the name from stdin when none is given
body:
## Problem

`greet.sh` requires the name as an argument. Piping into it does nothing —
`echo World | ./greet.sh` prints `greet: needs a name` and exits 2, which is
surprising when every other tool in the pipeline reads stdin.

## What to do

When no argument is given and stdin is not a terminal, read the name from the
first line of stdin and greet that. Keep the existing error for the case where
no argument is given and stdin *is* a terminal — that one is still a mistake.

An empty or blank first line counts as no name: keep the error and exit 2.

## Measure it

`./bench.sh` is the only throughput number this project has. It is slow — a
minute and a quarter, and it does not take a shorter mode. Run it once before
the change and once after, and quote both result lines in the PR body's
Verification section. Reading stdin puts a syscall in a path that had none, so
a regression here is the thing worth knowing about before the merge rather than
after.

## Done when

- `echo World | ./greet.sh` prints `Hello, World!` and exits 0.
- `./greet.sh` with a terminal on stdin still errors and exits 2.
- `./test.sh` passes, covering both.
- The PR body quotes a `./bench.sh` line from before the change and one from
  after, both of them numbers that were actually observed.
